newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to inaugurate gas pipeline section Dec 2.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to inaugurate gas pipeline section Dec 2.

text.p: Morocco will inaugurate on December 2 a gas pipeline section through which will flow 9.5 billion cubic metres annually from Algeria's Hassi R'mel to Spain via Morocco, an official said on Wednesday.

"A ceremony, which will bring together senior officials from Algeria, Morocco, Portugal and Spain, takes place in the northern city of Tangier on December 2, 1996," an official at the Moroccan energy ministry told Reuters.
Earlier this month, Algeria inaugurated the first section of the Maghreb-Europe gas pipeline built at an estimated cost of $2.3 billion over 30 months.

The pipeline, on which a first agreement was signed in 1991, runs 1,385 km (865 miles) from Algeria, through Morocco, under the Strait of Gibraltar, to the Spanish city of Cordoba, and is to link up with a gas distribution network for Portugal.
Officials said that by the year 2000, Algerian gas would cover 12 percent of Spain's energy consumption.
Algeria hopes to double its present annual gas exports to 60 billion cubic metres by the year 2000, when one Algerian official said its oil and gas exports should earn $16 billion.
Morocco later will use gas from Hassi R'mel, including some for electricity generation, when it has set up the infrastructure. Until then it will take royalties as a share of the income generated.
"A third inauguration ceremony is expected to take place in the Spanish city of Cordoba a week later," the official said.
The pipeline section in Portugal is expected to be operational in January 1997, officials said.
If this project is successful, another pipeline, totalling around 500 km (310 miles), may be needed to carry more gas from Hassi R'mel and then on to Europe.
